turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if the house in Belgrave Square was his property or if he rented it.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he rented the house in Belgrave Square and hoped that would not be a disqualification.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that renting property might be considered a temporary arrangement and asked if he owned any land or property in his own right.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned no land or property of his own and hoped that this would not affect his chances with Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that without substantial property or a significant social standing, Mr Worthing would be an unsuitable match for her daughter.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not let her engagement to Jack be determined by such superficial considerations as property and land.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that her daughter's happiness and future were too important to be left to the whims of someone who could not provide for her.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that her heart and happiness should be the determining factors in her marriage, not material possessions.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that in her world, a gentleman without a substantial fortune or a respectable lineage was hardly a suitable match, regardless of the depth of one’s heart.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not be swayed by societal expectations or material wealth, for true love and mutual respect were the only criteria worth considering.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that Gwendolen must understand that in the world of high society, a gentleman without means or a respectable background was hardly a suitable match, regardless of his supposed sentiments.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that Gwendolen must learn to prioritize practical considerations over emotional whims, as true happiness in life came from a stable marriage rather than fleeting infatuations.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not bend to her narrow views on marriage, for she valued Jack’s character and their love above all else.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted that Gwendolen must reconsider her decision, reminding her that a gentleman without a solid reputation and financial stability was not a fit match in their circles.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not compromise her principles for societal approval, for she believed in the sanctity of true love.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she would not allow her daughter to marry a man without proper connections and financial security, regardless of any romantic notions.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen insisted that she would follow her heart and marry Jack, despite her mother’s objections and societal expectations.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell insisted to Gwendolen that her decision to marry Jack was unacceptable and that she would not entertain such a notion, regardless of her daughter’s romantic ideals.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen insisted to her mother that she would not be swayed by social expectations and would marry Jack, no matter what objections were raised.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she would not permit her daughter to throw away her future on a man who lacked the proper background and means, regardless of the romantic fancies that clouded her judgment.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
